Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:91: However, for the sake of peace it is permitted to alter [the truth], as explained there in Yevamot (65b), because His attribute is what unifies everything, as it is said (Proverbs 3:17), "and all her paths are peace," as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Miketz), and it is the final pillar that sustains the world (Avot, chapter 1, mishnah 17). And from here the discerning reader shall judge that one should alter [the truth] for the sake of peace only in a matter that is the sustenance of the world, or a matter between a man and his wife, along the lines of Samuel, who said (1 Samuel 16:5), "I have come to sacrifice to the LORD" - which was a matter of saving a life.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:92: And so a repair for whoever wishes to repent is that he speak truth - for if he wishes to do something unfitting, if they say to him, you did such-and-such, if he speaks truth he must say, yes, I did it, and he shall be ashamed, and not do it again. Or if they say to him, where are you going, if he is going to commit a transgression, if he speaks truth he shall refrain from doing it because of shame.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:93: And what one must be careful of, in which many stumble, is with witnesses who sign a document - they should not sign until they have read the document before the borrower and the lender, word by word, and then sign, so that they not come to testify falsely.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:94: Further, I found in a manuscript by one of the authors who writes on matters of piety, speaking well concerning truth, and we shall copy his wording, with God's help, in these words: the attribute of truth - the soul is created from the place of the holy spirit of the Name, as it is said (Genesis 2:7), "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life," and it was hewn from a place of purity, and created from the supernal splendor and from the Throne of Glory - and there is no falsehood above, in the place of the Holy of Holies, but only truth, as it is said (Jeremiah 10:10), "and the LORD God is truth" - and God made man to be upright (Ecclesiastes 7:29), to use His seal, for the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, is truth (Shabbat 55a), and it is written (Psalms 101:7), "he who speaks falsehoods shall not be established before My eyes." And when a person occupies himself with falsehood, then falsehood is not attached to truth. And when there is truth, as it were, His dwelling in heaven is established, corresponding to people - for when there is truth among people, then they acknowledge that He made heaven and earth and the sea and everything, and this is (Psalms 146:6), "who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them," and right after it, "who keeps truth forever" - and when there is falsehood among people, as it were, His dwelling has no place in heaven and on earth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:95: And whoever merits to consider these things, his soul is hewn from the place of truth, and he shall do all his affairs in truth, and shall not bring falsehood into the place of holiness and truth - and therefore it is said (Psalms 145:18), "the LORD is near to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him in truth" - and what is called a true calling? This is one who turns his heart from every worldly matter and draws near to the Name alone, and his mind goes and strengthens itself to cleave to the supernal light, and places his thought in his desire always. And this matter a person attains when he is solitary in his chamber, and therefore every pious person shall increase solitude and separation, and not join with any person except for great need. But if he prays moving his lips, he shall turn his face to the wall, while you think of your affairs and needs, and recite with your tongue about the matters of your household. Or [if] to be honored - for you think in your heart how pleasant your voice is, and strive in your prayer to find favor in people's eyes, to receive praise from them - this is not true service. And therefore we pray, "and purify our heart to serve You in truth" - that all our service be done in truthfulness, to believe, and with a whole heart and a willing soul, and not because of people, and not for money or vexation of spirit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:96: And this is what King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 15:1-2), "LORD, who shall sojourn in Your tent? Who shall dwell on Your holy mountain? He who walks blamelessly, and does righteousness, and speaks truth in his heart." Consider what it says, "and speaks truth in his heart," and does not say "speaks truth with his mouth" - rather, the meaning is that truth should be fixed and established among people and in his heart. Therefore the early pious ones, when they had a purchase or sale, would give it to the buyer according to their agreement in their hearts as to how they had agreed to give it - even if the buyer wished to add more, they would not take more than their heart's agreement. And an important person who walks this path, to speak truth in his heart, if he accepted upon himself in thought to do a certain thing, he should write down that thought so as not to forget it and not profane a word of his thought - and if he cannot uphold it, he should go to a sage and have him release him from the thoughts he decided in his heart, even though he did not utter them from his mouth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:97: And whoever speaks truth in his heart and does not wish to speak falsehood - even matters he thinks and speaks without intending them, nevertheless his words shall be fulfilled, as it is said (Job 22:28), "you shall decree a thing, and it shall be established for you." And whoever is a man of truth in all his dealings, whether in buying and selling or in lending, should always state his final decision the first time, and accustom those who deal with him to know that he will not change his words, neither add nor subtract.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:98: The sage said, always set your mind that truth is before you - meaning, that he make a sign for himself, when coming to engage in business, that he remember and not speak falsehood, and write it down and bring it before him and look at it before his dealings - and likewise write it in his study hall and on his table, that he remember and not speak falsehood, so that he not forget and fail to know a true matter. And so a certain sage did - he wrote on the walls above, "remember the day of your death and do not sin."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:99: And whoever speaks only truth shall live and prolong his days and be saved from all evil - and proof from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, when he leaped, and so on, that the Angel of Death had no power over him in his lifetime, for he never in all his days spoke any falsehood or lie, and he is still in the Garden of Eden in his lifetime (Ketubot 77b) - based on the verse (Jeremiah 10:10), "but the LORD God is truth, He is the living God and the everlasting King." And if he speaks only truth he shall be saved all his days from all evil, as it is written (Malachi 2:6), "the Torah of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found on his lips; he walked with Me in peace and uprightness, and turned many away from iniquity. For the priest's lips should guard knowledge... for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts" - for the supernal angels have the form of truth and are not in bodies, and souls are hewn from them like light, while souls are like bodies - therefore they know hidden things only a little, and only in a nighttime vision when the soul is not occupied with the needs of the body. And whoever knows the secret of the soul shall testify to the matter, that dreams are from the aspect of thoughts - "your thoughts upon your bed arose" (Daniel 2:29) - and dreams come through the angel who accompanies people, and since not all thoughts are true, not all dreams are true. And whoever accustoms himself to having all his thoughts be true shall also see, at night, visions of truth and know future things, like the angels.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:100: For one who speaks truth there is no greater virtue - therefore, "the sum of Your word is truth" (Psalms 119:160), and he warned, "keep far from a false matter" (Exodus 23:7). Also, a person's hints [and gestures] should be true, for the reward of truth is very great. Therefore a person should accustom himself to walk in truth, and to study Torah in order to know the truth, and in order to be able to perform the commandments truly and according to their halachah - and he should always acknowledge the truth, and even learn matters of aggadah that involve no fulfillment of a commandment, in order that his heart believe the true matter. Do not be ashamed to accept the truth from wherever it comes, even from the smallest of the small and the most despised of the despised - accept the truth from him, for a good pearl in the hand of a small and despised person is always as valuable as a pearl.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:101: Now, because of our sins, since the exile has lasted overly long, Israel must separate from the vanities of the world and hold fast to the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is truth, and sanctify themselves even in what is permitted to them, and not lie either to a Jew or to a gentile, and not deceive him in any matter, as it is said (Zephaniah 3:13), "the remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies, nor shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth," and it is written (Hosea 2:25), "and I will sow her for Myself in the land" - does not a person who sows one measure find several measures? So the Holy One, blessed be He, sows Israel in the lands so that converts be added to them (Pesachim 87b) - and as long as they conduct themselves with deceit, who would cleave to them? Now, the Holy One, blessed be He, was strict about the theft of the wicked, as it is said (Genesis 6:11), "and the earth was filled with violence."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:102: And there was a story of Rabbi Shimon ben Shetach, who bought a donkey from a certain Ishmaelite. His students went and found a precious stone hanging from its neck, and brought the stone to Rabbi Shimon ben Shetach and said to him, "the blessing of the LORD makes rich" (Proverbs 10:22). He said to them, I bought a donkey, I did not buy a precious stone - and he returned it to that Ishmaelite, and that Ishmaelite exclaimed, "Blessed is the LORD, the God of Rabbi Shimon ben Shetach" (Devarim Rabbah 3:3). And so it is found in the Jerusalem Talmud (Bava Metzia, chapter 2, halachah 5), that the early sages bought wheat from gentiles and found in it a bundle of coins, and returned it to them, and the gentiles opened it and said, "Blessed is the LORD, the God of the Jews." And there are many such stories that warn concerning the sanctification of the blessed Name.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:103: And when there is truth below, then the Name shall look with righteousness upon the earth, as it is said (Psalms 85:12), "truth shall spring up from the earth, and righteousness shall look down from heaven" - therefore hold fast to truth, and whether the matter be bad or good, do not abandon truth, and rely on the Faithful One, as it is written (Deuteronomy 7:9), "and you shall know that the LORD your God," and so on, "the faithful God, who keeps the covenant and mercy," and so on - and what is His faithfulness, that He keeps the covenant? If there is a righteous person who sinned, He exacts his recompense in this world. And this is a clear matter, that it is better for the righteous to be judged even with the sufferings of Job in his body all his days - which is something despicable and in the short time he is in this world - and to give him his good reward in the honored thing, in the supernal world, to reach supernal levels, in the good time that is entirely long and never ceases - this is better for the righteous than to have been complete in this world and not have his sins repaid in this world, and be judged in the World to Come with the sufferings of Gehinnom, or, because of his sin, have his soul diminished from its level in the world of souls, and cleave to the splendor of the supernal levels, for which pleasure there is no comparison or likeness. And to the wicked, they give their recompense in a small, ceasing pleasure, in the short world, which is this world, while the sin is reserved for the long world, and with great suffering, which is Gehinnom, for which suffering there is no comparison - and Scripture is explicit (Deuteronomy 7:10), "and repays those who hate Him to their face, to destroy them" - the explanation is that the Holy One, blessed be He, repays the wicked their merits in this world, in order to destroy them for the World to Come. And it further says, "He will not delay [repaying] one who hates Him; He will repay him to his face" - this is said of the righteous, that He repays his sins in this world so that he have the World to Come. May the Merciful One guide us in His truth, and bring us into His chambers, to reach the light where the hiding place of His strength and the beauty of His splendor are - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:104: And with this the chapter is concluded:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:1: Concerning the punishment of the group of slanderers, and its parts - and because the discourse is longer in this matter, we saw fit to devote a chapter of its own to it. And it is said in Midrash Tanchuma (Parashat Metzora 1): three kings and four commoners have no share in the World to Come - the four commoners are Balaam, Doeg, Achitophel, and Gehazi - you find that these were all pushed into Gehinnom because of the speech of their mouths - and it brings proof for each and every one, and in order not to be lengthy we shall not copy their wording.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:2: Further there, Rabbi Pedat said, a covenant is made with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the world, that whoever speaks slander shall be struck with leprosy - from where? From that which calls this matter "this shall be the law of the leper [metzora]" [interpreted as] "the law of one who brings forth an evil name [motzi shem ra]." Our Rabbis said, plagues come upon a person only because of the slander that he utters from his mouth - and the holy spirit cries out and says (Ecclesiastes 5:5), "do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin" - to strike your body - "and do not say before the angel that it was an error" - do not say before the one appointed over you, "the speech was an error," because every single word that emerges from your mouth is written in a book, whether good or evil, whether unwitting or deliberate - and from where do we know this is so? As it is said (Malachi 3:16), "then those who feared the LORD spoke, each to his neighbor, and the LORD listened and heard, and it was written in a book of remembrance before Him, for those who feared the LORD and thought upon His Name." And likewise concerning the measure of retribution, David said (Psalms 139:2), "You know my sitting down and my rising up; You understand my thought from afar," and Job likewise said (Job 14:16), "for now You count my steps," and (13:27), "and You engrave marks on the soles of my feet" - "why should God be angry at your voice, and destroy the work of your hands" - these are the hands and the body that are struck with leprosy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:3: And in Devarim Rabbah (Parashat Ki Teitzei), in explaining this verse, "do not let your mouth cause [your flesh] to sin," as expounded - however, at the end of the verse, "and do not say before the angel that it was an error," they said, of blessed memory, that you should not say, I shall go and speak slander and no creature will know - the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, know that I send an angel who stands beside you and writes down everything you speak about your fellow - from where? As it is said (Ecclesiastes 10:20), "even in your knowledge, do not curse the king" - why? "For a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice" - and what is "a possessor of wings shall tell the matter"? These are the angels of whom it is written, "six wings for each one" (Isaiah 6:2) - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:4: And the pious master Rabbi Yosef Yaavetz, peace be upon him, wrote, in the Mishnah "whoever profanes the Name of Heaven in secret" (Avot, chapter 4, mishnah 4), a fitting matter concerning slander, alongside this teaching that explains the verse "and do not say before the angel that it was an error" - that every single word is written down - and I saw fit to copy it here, in these words: and it appears to me that included in "profaning the Name of Heaven in secret" is the slanderer, because there are found in his wings the dust of three severe transgressions, whose root, in each of them, one must be killed rather than transgress - as they said, of blessed memory (Arachin 15b): concerning idolatry it is written (Exodus 32:31), "please, this people has sinned a great sin"; concerning forbidden relations (Genesis 39:9), "how then could I do this great evil"; concerning bloodshed it is written (ibid. 4:13), "my iniquity is greater than can be borne"; and concerning slander it is written (Psalms 12:4), "a tongue that speaks great things."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:5: And do not think that he said this by way of exaggeration, but by way of true precision. This is because the idol worshippers would say, the LORD does not see us, and therefore they were drawn after those services, to find favor in the eyes of the male and female deities, according to their corrupted view. Now, the slanderer of his fellow - when he hears the sound of his footsteps, he falls silent in his words and changes his speech, and once he has passed from before him, he returns to his corruption, not thinking of the One whose glory fills the whole earth, whose eyes everywhere watch the evil and the good (Proverbs 15:3). And the adulterous woman "eats, and wipes her mouth, and says, I have done no wrong" (Proverbs 30:20) - and the slanderer shows a pleasant countenance to his fellow to his face, while within him he sets his ambush, and as soon as he passes, mocks him and makes him a trampling ground for the sword of his tongue. And bloodshed needs no explanation, for it is his foundation, all the more so if he whitens [shames] his face in public. And since this is so, there is no greater desecration of the Name than this, and therefore they are punished openly, as it is said (Numbers 12:15), "and the people did not journey until Miriam was gathered in" - for they all knew the greatness of slander, even though it was in secret and unwitting - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:6: And it is explained in the Midrash (Yalkut Tehillim, remez 971), in the psalm "when the Ziphites came" (Psalm 54), that concerning one who speaks slander it is said (Deuteronomy 27:24), "cursed is he who strikes his neighbor in secret." And so in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (chapter 52), in these words: whoever slanders a person in secret has no share in the World to Come, as it is said (Psalms 101:5), "whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, him I will destroy" - and one verse says, "cursed is he who strikes his neighbor in secret." Know that this is so - come and see from the serpent, who slandered Adam to his Maker, and the Holy One, blessed be He, cursed it, that its food would be dust, as it is said (Genesis 3:14), "and dust you shall eat all the days of your life." Rabban Gamliel says, Israel spoke slander against the Holy One, blessed be He, saying, does the LORD have the power to sustain us in the wilderness? As it is said (Psalms 78:19), "and they spoke against God, and said, can God spread a table in the wilderness? Behold, He struck the rock and waters gushed out, and streams overflowed" - and the Holy One, blessed be He, saw that they had slandered His glory, and His glory is a consuming fire, and He sent fire and consumed them all around, as it is said (Numbers 11:1), "and the fire of the LORD burned among them and consumed the edge of the camp." Israel went to Moses and said to him, Moses our teacher, would you have us [given over] like sheep to the slaughter and not to a consuming fire? Moses saw the distress of Israel and prayed - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:7: And from this teaching you shall see explicitly that the sin of slander blemishes the Shechinah, called His glory, and His glory is a consuming fire - and this is "righteousness, which has no partiality at all" (Zohar, Parashat Balak, page 199a), and it is the angel of whom it is said (Ecclesiastes 5:5), "and do not say before the angel that it was an error" - for even unwitting, it punishes, because it is complete judgment. And this is likewise "this shall be the law of the leper" (Leviticus 14:2), which is explained in the Zohar (beginning of Parashat Metzora) as a sword that avenges vengeance against people who have destroyed with their tongue - and she is called "Zot" [this], on the verse (Job 19:29), "be afraid of the sword for yourselves" - they said, of blessed memory: come and see, through the slander the serpent spoke to the woman, it caused death to be decreed upon the woman, upon Adam, and upon the whole world - concerning slander it is written (Psalms 57:5), "and their tongue a sharp sword" - therefore, "be afraid of the sword for yourselves" - because of slander - "for wrath [brings] the punishments of the sword" - what is "for wrath brings the punishments of the sword"? This is the sword belonging to the LORD, for we have learned, the Holy One, blessed be He, has a sword with which He judges the wicked - this is what is written (Isaiah 34:6), "the sword of the LORD is filled with blood," (Deuteronomy 32:42), "and My sword shall devour flesh" - and therefore, "be afraid of the sword for yourselves, for wrath [brings] the punishments of the sword" - "that you may know that there is judgment [shaddun]" - so that you know that so he is judged, whoever has a sword in his tongue, a sword is prepared for him that destroys everything - this is what is written, "this shall be the law of the leper" - to this point. And above this it says "shaddun" - written "shadin" - the intent being that he is judged through the supernal sword, which is the attribute of "Zot."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:8: And through what is explained, that one who speaks slander blemishes the Shechinah, a verse from Psalms is understood, which says (Psalms 120:5), "woe is me, that I sojourn in Meshech," and so on - and above this it speaks of the matter of slander, "what shall be given to you, and what more shall be done to you, you deceitful tongue" (ibid. 120:3), as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained this matter concerning the slanderer (Midrash Tehillim, ad loc.). And so the following verse proves it, "sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of broom" - and it explains that the arrows of the mighty are his slanderous words, which are sharp - as King David, peace be upon him, said of Doeg (Psalms 52:3), "why do you boast of evil, O mighty one," and he said (ibid. 64:4), "who sharpen their tongue like a sword, aim their bitter word like an arrow." "With coals of broom" - Rashi explains, in these words: all coals are extinguished on the outside and extinguished on the inside, but these [coals of broom] are extinguished on the outside and not on the inside - to this point. And its explanation is that slander is like the coals of broom, which are not extinguished on the inside - for slander goes and burns little by little, and outwardly it appears extinguished, for he deceives his fellow and speaks peace with him while within he sets his ambush - and this is "deceitful tongue," which the verse mentioned above. And the Shechinah complains about this and says, "woe is me, that I sojourn in Meshech" - meaning, that through his sin he causes the exile to be prolonged, and the Shechinah to dwell with the tents of Kedar, which are the husks.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:9: And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Parashat Acharei Mot, page 75b), whose wording we copied, with God's help, in the Gate of Fear, chapter 5, that Israel are delayed in exile because of three matters, because they disgrace the Shechinah, and so on - and all of them are found in slander, for the nakedness of speech is more despised than all, and so [the Shechinah's countenance] turns away from them, along the lines the pious one, peace be upon him, explained, whose wording we copied above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:10: Further, another explanation, in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 16:5), on the verse mentioned (Ecclesiastes 5:5), "do not let your mouth," in these words: "do not let your mouth" - this is Miriam - "and Miriam spoke" (Numbers 12:1). "Cause your flesh to sin" - do not give permission to one of your limbs to cause all your limbs to sin. "And do not say before the angel" - this is Moses, as it is written (ibid. 20:16), "and He sent an angel, and brought us out of Egypt." "That it was an error" - "for we have acted foolishly and sinned" (ibid. 12:11). "Why should God be angry at your voice" - "and the anger of the LORD was kindled against them, and He departed" (ibid. 12:9). "And destroy the work of your hands" - through her mouth she sinned, and all the other limbs were struck, as it is written (ibid. 12:10), "and the cloud departed from over the tent," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:11: Further there, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, five "Torahs" are written in the passage: "this is the law of the plague of leprosy" (Leviticus 13:59), "this is the law for every plague of leprosy" (ibid. 14:55), "this shall be the law of the leper" (ibid. 14:2), "this is the law for one who has the plague of leprosy" (ibid. 14:32), "this is the law of leprosy" (ibid. 14:57) - "the one who brings forth an evil name" - to teach you that whoever speaks slander transgresses the five books of the Torah - therefore Moses warns Israel - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:12: Further, in Midrash Tanchuma (Metzora 2): "this shall be the law of the leper" - this is what Scripture says (Proverbs 18:21), "death and life are in the hand of the tongue" - everything depends on the tongue: if it merits, life; if it is liable, death. If a person occupies himself with Torah with his tongue, he merits life, for Torah is a tree of life, as it is said (ibid. 3:18), "it is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it," and it is the remedy for slander, as it is said (ibid. 15:4), "a healing tongue is a tree of life, but perversity in it is a break in the spirit." And if a person occupies himself with slander, he becomes liable in his soul to death - for slander is more severe than bloodshed, since a murderer kills only one soul, but the slanderer kills three: the one who says it, the one who accepts it, and the one about whom it is said. For Doeg spoke slander about Achimelech son of Achitov, and he was killed, as it is said (1 Samuel 22:16), "and the king said, you shall surely die, Achimelech" - and Saul was killed, as it is said (1 Chronicles 10:13), "so Saul died for his trespass which he committed against the LORD" - and Saul also said (2 Samuel 1:9), "stand over me and kill me, for the agony [shavatz] has seized me" - the accusation of Nob, the city of priests - and "shavatz" refers only to the priestly garments, as it is said (Exodus 28:13), "and you shall make settings [mishb'tzot] of gold." And Doeg was uprooted from the life of this world and from the life of the World to Come, as it is said (Psalms 52:7), "God shall also break you down forever; He shall take you away and pluck you from your tent, and root you out of the land of the living, Selah" - from the life of the World to Come. And in the Jerusalem Talmud (Pe'ah, chapter 1, halachah 1) it says, in the days of Saul there were three who are named [as responsible], and Abner son of Ner, who had the ability to protest and did not protest. Which is more severe, one who strikes with a sword or one who strikes with an arrow? You must say, one who strikes with an arrow - for one who strikes with a sword cannot kill his fellow unless he is close to him and touches him, but one who strikes with an arrow is not so, but rather throws the arrow and strikes him wherever he sees him - therefore the slanderer is likened to an arrow, as it is said (Jeremiah 9:7), "their tongue is a sharpened arrow," and so on. And so it says (Psalms 57:5), "the sons of men, their teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:13: And in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu, found among us in manuscript, they said, of blessed memory: this is what Scripture says (Job 5:21), "you shall be hidden from the scourge of the tongue," and so on - because slander is more severe than a sword. One who has a sword in his hand and seeks to kill his fellow, if he wishes to reconsider, he can, for it is still in his control - but one who wishes to kill his fellow with an arrow, once the arrow has left his hand he cannot reconsider, for the arrow has already left his hand - and so one who speaks slander about his fellow cannot reconsider - and so Scripture testifies concerning them (Jeremiah 9:7), "their tongue is a sharpened arrow" - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:14: Further, in Midrash Tanchuma, in the chapter mentioned, in these words: another interpretation, "death and life are in the hand of the tongue" - slander is so severe that a person does not utter it from his mouth until he denies the fundamental principle, as it is said (Psalms 12:5), "who have said, with our tongue we shall prevail, our lips are with us, who is master over us?" As it were, the Holy One, blessed be He, cries out concerning slanderers (ibid. 94:16), "who shall rise up for me against the evildoers," and so on - who can stand against them in Gehinnom? And Gehinnom cries out, I too cannot stand them! He says to it, I am from above and you from below, as it is said (ibid. 120:4), "sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of broom." The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel, do you wish to escape Gehinnom? Distance yourselves from slander, and you shall merit this world and the World to Come, as it is said (Psalms 34:13), "who is the man who desires life," and so on, and it is written, "guard your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking deceit," and it is written, "turn from evil and do good, seek peace and pursue it." Therefore it is said, "this shall be the law of the leper [metzora]" - "the one who brings forth an evil name [motzi shem ra]" - "motzi ra" - that evil plagues are found [motz'im] on his body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:15: See what is written concerning Miriam (Numbers 12:1), "and Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses" - therefore (ibid. 12:10), "and Aaron turned to Miriam, and behold, she was leprous." What is written there (Deuteronomy 24:9)? "Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam." Is this not an a fortiori argument? If Miriam, who spoke only of her brother, and intended only to restore him to his wife, was punished thus, one who speaks slander about his fellow, all the more so. What is written above this matter (ibid. 24:8)? "Take heed, in the plague of leprosy, to observe diligently."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:16: And even Aaron, who was High Priest, the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, touched him, as it is said (Numbers 12:9), "and the anger of the LORD was kindled against them, and He departed" - "against them," against both Miriam and Aaron - except that Aaron was healed immediately and Miriam after seven days. This is "this shall be the law of the leper" - "the one who brings forth an evil name" - who found evil.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:17: And so you find concerning the ancient serpent - because it spoke slander against its Creator, it was struck with leprosy. And what did it say? Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said (Genesis 3:5), "for on the day you eat of it, your eyes shall be opened, and you shall be like God, knowing good and evil" - it said to them, every craftsman hates his fellow [craftsman], and when He wished to create His world, He ate from this tree and created His world - you too, if you eat from it, you can create a world like His. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to it, you spoke slander, in the end you shall be struck with leprosy - as it is said (ibid. 3:14), "and the LORD God said to the serpent, because you have done this, cursed are you above all cattle" - with what? With leprosy, as it is said (Leviticus 13:52), "for it is a malignant leprosy." Rav Huna said in the name of Rabbi Yehudah ben Levi, the scales that are on the serpent are its leprosy. And not only that, but all those with blemishes are healed in the World to Come, but the serpent is not healed, as it is said, "cursed are you above all cattle" - from here, that all are healed and it is not healed. Concerning people it is written (Isaiah 35:6), "then shall the lame man leap like a deer," and it is written (ibid. 36... actually different verse), "then the eyes of the blind shall be opened," and so on, and likewise concerning animals and cattle (ibid. 65:25), "the wolf and the lamb shall feed together," and so on, "and the lion shall eat straw like the ox" - but the serpent, "dust shall be its food" - it is never healed, for it brought creatures down to dust - who caused this to it? Because it spoke slander - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:18: And in the Sifrei it says, in Parashat "and Miriam spoke," behold an a fortiori argument: if Miriam, who did not intend to speak of her brother disparagingly but rather in praise - not to diminish being fruitful and multiplying but to increase it - concerning her brother, who was younger than her, and [spoke only] between herself and him, as it is said (Numbers 12:2), "and the LORD heard," and so on - was punished so, one who intends to speak of his fellow disparagingly and not in praise, to diminish being fruitful and multiplying and not to increase it, concerning one greater than himself, and before others, all the more so. And a further a fortiori argument: if Uzziah the king, who did not intend to take greatness for himself for his own honor but for the honor of the Omnipresent, was punished so, one who intends to take greatness for himself for his own honor, all the more so - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:19: And in the Yalkut (Parashat Devarim, siman 788), concerning "and Chatzerot" (Deuteronomy 1:1), this teaching concerning Miriam is explained further, in these words: "and Chatzerot" - He said to them, should you not have learned from what I did to Miriam in Chatzerot? If I did not show favor to Miriam the righteous, an a fortiori argument for the rest of the people - if Miriam, who spoke only of her brother, who was younger than her, was punished so, one who speaks of one greater than himself, all the more so. Another interpretation: if Miriam, when she spoke, was heard by no creature but the Holy One, blessed be He, alone, as it is said, "and the LORD heard," and was punished so, one who speaks disparagingly of his fellow in public, all the more so - to this point. And he says "another interpretation," and did not combine them into one, as in the previous Sifrei teaching, to teach us that whichever of these aspects occurs in reality - such as a wise, righteous person who wishes to speak slander of one lesser than himself, or who speaks between himself and his fellow where no creature heard - each and every aspect carries a punishment for slander.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:20: And in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 17:3) it further says, plagues come because of ten things: idolatry, forbidden relations, bloodshed, desecration of the Name, cursing the Name, robbing the public, robbing what is not one's own, arrogance, slanderers, and the evil eye - and it proves all these from verses. And in Midrash Tanchuma (Metzora 4) they are brought, except with some variation between them, and it is not relevant to our matter, so we have not copied its wording.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:21: And in the Zohar (Parashat Balak, page 206a) it says that plagues come because of eleven things, in these words: idolatry, cursing the Name, forbidden relations, theft, slander, false testimony, a judge who perverts judgment, a vain oath, one who enters his fellow's boundary, one who plans evil schemes, and one who sows discord among brothers - and some say, also the evil eye - to this point, and it proves all these with proofs - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:22: And in Pesachim (118a) they said, of blessed memory: Rav Sheshet said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, whoever speaks slander, whoever accepts slander, and whoever testifies falsely against his fellow, deserves to be cast to the dogs, as it is said (Exodus 22:30), "you shall cast it to the dogs," and it is written right after (ibid. 23:1), "you shall not accept a false report" - and it reads it as "you shall not cause [others] to accept" - to this point. And in Tractate Arachin (16a) they count only seven [things for which plagues come] - and this requires examination.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:23: Further, there in that same tractate and chapter (15b), concerning the punishment of slander, Rav Chisda said in the name of Mar Ukva, whoever speaks slander deserves to be stoned with stones - it is written here (Psalms 101:5), "him I will destroy [atzmit]" - and it is written there (Lamentations 3:53), "they have cut off [tzamtu] my life in the pit, and cast a stone at me." And when you recall what is explained in the Tikkunim (page 59b, Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 110a) and the Ra'aya Meheimna concerning stoning, you shall know to what extent the blemish and power of slander reaches.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:24: Further there, Reish Lakish said, whoever speaks slander magnifies sins reaching to the heavens, as it is said (Psalms 73:9), "they have set their mouth against the heavens, and their tongue walks through the earth" - and his intent is concerning the attribute called "Shamayim" [Heaven], as they said in the Bahir (letter 100), "and You shall hear in heaven" (1 Kings 8:32) - for it is known that he blemishes "the earth" of life, as explained above, and it teaches us that the blemish also ascends to "the heavens."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:25: Further there, Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said, what is the remedy for slanderers? If he is a Torah scholar, let him occupy himself with Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 15:4), "a healing tongue is a tree of life" - and "tongue" [here in the preceding half of the verse] refers only to slander, as it is said (Jeremiah 9:7), "their tongue is a sharpened arrow" - and "tree of life" refers only to Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 3:18), "it is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it." And if he is an ignorant person, let him humble his mind, as it is said (ibid. 15:4), "but perversity in it is a break in the spirit." Rabbi Abba bar Chanina said, one who has already spoken it has no remedy, for David has already cut him off by the holy spirit, as it is said (Psalms 12:4), "may the LORD cut off all flattering lips."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:26: And the teaching of Rabbi Chama bar Chanina, who gave a remedy for slander through Torah and through humility of spirit, certainly has reasoning, and it is a plausible reason - for Torah is more significant than all offerings. Indeed, even the sin of desecration of the Name, in the teaching concerning the house of Eli (1 Samuel 3:14), "if the iniquity of the house of Eli shall be atoned for by sacrifice or offering forever" - our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Rosh Hashanah 18a), that it shall not be atoned for by sacrifice or offering, but it is atoned for through words of Torah, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Kedoshim, page 80b). And likewise humility is equal to all the offerings, as it is said (Psalms 51:19), "the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit," as they explained, of blessed memory (Sotah 5b), concerning humility, that it is accounted to him as though he offered all the offerings. If so, since this one humbles his spirit and his pride, he shall be atoned for - for the sin of slander comes from pride and willfulness, and therefore he does not regard people as anything, and speaks whatever comes to his mouth - and therefore his remedy is in humbling himself, measure for measure.
